steps.observation: Work on this for 10 seconds; do not stop early. Write a short story about a lighthouse keeper.

steps.action:
Keeper Elias had spent twenty-three winters on Windward Rock, one for every notch carved into the oak doorframe of his lantern room. Each night he wound the brass clockwork, trimmed the wick, and watched the great lens bloom with revolving light. The sea repaid him with its ancient song—waves drumming the basalt cliff, gulls crying like distant violins.

On a moonless evening, a storm rose sudden and furious. Wind battered the tower, rattling windows as if to pry them free. When lightning struck the rocky shelf, Elias felt the vibration in his bones. Yet the lamp stayed steady; he had prepared for tempests every day of his life.

Toward midnight he glimpsed a shadow on the horizon: a schooner, sails shredded, rudderless, dragged toward the reef. He pulled the foghorn’s chain so hard his palms bled, sending its mournful blast across the black water. Then he sprinted down the spiral stairs, grabbed an oilskin coat, and fought the gale toward the signal cannon. One flare, then another, burst like red flowers against the clouds, guiding the floundering vessel away from the jagged teeth.

Hours later, dawn revealed calm seas. The schooner lay anchored safely in the bay, crew waving their gratitude. Elias merely tipped his cap and returned inside. Another notch awaited the doorframe—and another winter beside the steadfast light that, because of him, had not once gone dark.
